relearning.title: Read: predicting what a mutation does
relearning.description: A short reading with the three-letter-word sentence analogy, worked examples and quick checks.

body.text:
**I can predict the effects of mutations on DNA.**

**Think of a sentence made only of three-letter words:** THE CAT ATE THE RAT. Each word is like a codon. Now make one mistake.

**Swap one letter:** THE CAT ATE THE **H**AT. One word changes, and the rest still reads fine. This is a **substitution** (also called a **point mutation**): one base is swapped for another.

**Delete one letter** (the C in CAT): THE ATA TET HER AT. Every word after the mistake turns into nonsense, because the reading groups shifted. This is a **frameshift mutation**, caused by an **insertion** (adding a base) or a **deletion** (removing a base).

**A mutation** is any change in the DNA sequence. Because DNA → mRNA → protein, a change in the DNA can change the protein.

**What a substitution can do:**
- **Silent:** the new codon codes for the same amino acid, so the protein does not change.
- **Missense:** one amino acid changes.
- **Nonsense:** the new codon is a stop codon, so the protein is cut short.

**Worked example (sickle cell):** Part of the normal mRNA for hemoglobin is AUG GAG AAA = Met – Glu – Lys. A substitution changes GAG to **GUG**. Codons: GAG = Glu, GUG = Val. The chain becomes **Met – Val – Lys**. One amino acid changed, and that one change makes red blood cells bend into a sickle shape.

checks.prompt: The mRNA AUG UUU GGA changes to AUG UUC GGA. Both UUU and UUC code for Phe. What happens to the protein?

options.text: Nothing changes (a silent mutation)
One amino acid changes
The protein stops early

checks.explanation: UUU and UUC both code for Phe, so the chain is still Met – Phe – Gly. A change in the DNA does not always change the protein.

checks.prompt: Which mutation will most likely change the protein the most?

options.text: Swapping one base near the end of the gene
Swapping one base that makes a silent mutation
Deleting one base near the start of the gene

checks.explanation: Deleting a base causes a frameshift, so every codon after it changes. Near the start, that is almost the whole protein. A swap changes one codon at most.

sections.title: Frameshifts, chromosomes and causes

body.text:
**Worked example 2 (frameshift):** The mRNA AUG GCA UUA CGA codes for Met – Ala – Leu – Arg. Delete the G at the start of the second codon. The bases now regroup as AUG CAU UAC GA. Codons: CAU = His, UAC = Tyr. The chain becomes **Met – His – Tyr**, and every amino acid after the deletion changed.

**Worked example 3 (nonsense):** The mRNA AUG UAC GGA codes for Met – Tyr – Gly. A substitution changes UAC to **UAA**, a stop codon. The chain is now just **Met**, then stop. A protein cut that short usually can't do its job.

**Inserting or deleting three bases** adds or removes one whole codon. The reading frame stays the same, so it is not a frameshift. Only one amino acid is added or lost.

**Chromosomal mutations** change big pieces of a chromosome: a **deletion** loses a piece, a **duplication** copies a piece, an **inversion** flips a piece backward, and a **translocation** moves a piece to a different chromosome.

**What causes mutations?** Some are copying mistakes during DNA replication. Others come from **mutagens**: UV light from the sun, X-rays, and chemicals like those in cigarette smoke.

**Effects can be harmful, neutral or helpful.** Most are neutral or harmful, but some help an organism survive, and those add the variation that evolution works on.

**Watch out for:** thinking every mutation changes the protein (silent ones do not), thinking a frameshift only changes one amino acid, calling a three-base insertion a frameshift, and thinking all mutations are harmful.

checks.prompt: The mRNA AUG AAA UGG changes to AUG AAA UGA. UGG = Trp and UGA = stop. What kind of mutation is this?

options.text: Silent: the protein stays the same
Nonsense: the protein is cut short
Missense: one amino acid is swapped

checks.explanation: UGA is a stop codon, so the chain ends after Met – Lys. A substitution that makes a stop codon is a nonsense mutation. Calling it missense misses that no amino acid takes Trp's place.

checks.prompt: Inserting or deleting one base shifts how every codon after it is read. What is this kind of mutation called?
checks.explanation: It is a frameshift mutation, because the three-base reading frame shifts. A substitution changes only one codon, so it is not a frameshift.

sections.shortAnswer: Explain why a deletion of one base usually changes a protein more than a substitution of one base.

relearning.title: Do: find the mutation and predict its effect
relearning.description: Two worked problems that reveal one step at a time: a substitution, then a frameshift.

body.problem: Normal DNA: TAC CTT TTT ACT. Mutated DNA: TAC CAT TTT ACT. Predict the effect on the protein. Codons you need: AUG = Met, GAA = Glu, GUA = Val, AAA = Lys, UGA = stop.

steps.text: Find the difference. Compare base by base: the second triplet changed from CTT to CAT. One T was swapped for an A, so this is a substitution.
Transcribe both strands (DNA A → U, T → A, C → G, G → C). Normal mRNA: AUG GAA AAA UGA. Mutated mRNA: AUG GUA AAA UGA.
Translate both. Normal: Met – Glu – Lys, then stop. Mutated: Met – Val – Lys, then stop.
Predict the effect. One amino acid changed (Glu → Val), so this is a missense mutation. The protein may fold into a different shape and work poorly, like hemoglobin in sickle cell disease.

checks.prompt: Your turn: transcribe the mutated DNA triplet CAT into mRNA.
checks.explanation: C→G, A→U, T→A gives GUA. Writing GTA is the common mistake: mRNA uses U, not T.

checks.prompt: A substitution changes the codon GAA (Glu) to GAG (also Glu). What is the effect on the protein?

options.text: No change: it is a silent mutation
One amino acid changes: it is a missense mutation
Every amino acid after it changes: it is a frameshift

checks.explanation: Both codons code for Glu, so the protein is the same. A substitution never shifts the reading frame, so it can't be a frameshift.

body.problem: Normal DNA: TAC GGT AAT CCG ATT. A mutation deletes the first G of the second triplet. Predict the effect. Codons you need: AUG = Met, CCA = Pro, UUA = Leu, GGC = Gly, CAU = His, UAA, UAG and UGA = stop.

steps.text: Translate the normal gene first. mRNA: AUG CCA UUA GGC UAA. Protein: Met – Pro – Leu – Gly, then stop.
Delete the base. The DNA is now TACGTAATCCGATT. Regroup it in threes from the start: TAC GTA ATC CGA TT.
Transcribe the mutated DNA: AUG CAU UAG GCU AA.
Translate: AUG = Met, CAU = His, and UAG is a stop codon. The protein is just Met – His, then stop.
Predict the effect. Removing one base shifted the reading frame, so every codon after it changed, and a stop codon showed up early. This frameshift makes a short, broken protein.

checks.prompt: Your turn: in the mutated DNA TAC GTA ATC, transcribe the third triplet ATC into mRNA.
checks.explanation: A→U, T→A, C→G gives UAG, which is a stop codon. Writing TAG is the common mistake: mRNA uses U.

checks.prompt: Which one-base mutation near the start of a gene would most likely cause the least harm?

options.text: Deleting one base
Substituting one base
Inserting one base

checks.explanation: A substitution changes one codon at most, and it might even be silent. Deleting or inserting one base causes a frameshift that changes every codon after it.

checks.prompt: THE CAT ATE THE RAT becomes THE CAT ATE THE BAT. Which kind of mutation is this like?

options.text: A frameshift caused by an insertion
A substitution (point mutation)
A frameshift caused by a deletion

checks.explanation: One letter was swapped and only one word changed, so it is a substitution. A frameshift would turn every word after the mistake into nonsense.

checks.prompt: A piece of a chromosome breaks off and attaches to a different chromosome. Which chromosomal mutation is this?

options.text: Deletion
Duplication
Inversion
Translocation

checks.explanation: A translocation moves a piece to a different chromosome. An inversion flips a piece backward on the same chromosome.

sections.title: Mutations: Silent, Missense, Nonsense, and Frameshift

checks.prompt: The mRNA AUG CAU GGA changes to AUG CGU GGA. CAU = His and CGU = Arg. What kind of mutation is this?

options.text: Silent: the protein stays the same
Nonsense: the protein is cut short
Missense: one amino acid changes

checks.explanation: One base was swapped and the codon now codes for a different amino acid (His → Arg), so it is missense. It is not silent, because the amino acid changed.

checks.prompt: Three bases are inserted in the middle of a gene. What is the most likely effect on the protein?

options.text: One amino acid is added, and the rest stay the same
Every amino acid after the insertion changes
The protein does not change at all

checks.explanation: Three bases add one whole codon, so the reading frame stays the same. Calling a three-base insertion a frameshift is the common mistake.

sections.shortAnswer: A substitution near the start of a gene changes one codon into a stop codon. Name this kind of mutation and predict what happens to the protein.
